page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual machine configured with high-speed local NVMe storage and enhanced networking throughput. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio typical of AWS general-purpose tiers. It features a 54 MB L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware integration differentiates the m6idn family via bundled ephemeral storage and high network capacity. The instance includes 1,900 GB of directly attached local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. In benchmark testing, the system achieves average-tier performance across varied computational tasks, scoring 1,633 on Geekbench single-core and 13,967 on multi-core, alongside a multi-core stress-ng result of 30,911.76. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 146.7 GB/s, while write operations reach 67.89 GB/s.

Data pipeline and serving evaluations show strong throughput figures, registering 30.66 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 31.29 GB/s in static web serving throughput. CPU-bound inference tests demonstrate capability for small to medium models, producing 260.68 tokens per second on a 135M model and 19.68 tokens per second on a 7B model. Larger parameter execution (70B) falls into the lower quartile at 6.05 tokens per second for prompt processing, reflecting the absence of hardware accelerators.

The m6idn.8xlarge offers cost-efficient balance when workloads simultaneously saturate CPU, system memory, high network bandwidth, and low-latency disk I/O. Because ephemeral NVMe storage is bundled, it reduces reliance on network-attached EBS volumes for temporary file manipulation. Primary workload fits include relational and non-relational database nodes, distributed caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and real-time log ingestion systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 32 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 1,900 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, it provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate solid middle-tier processing capabilities, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 35,392.93 and Geekbench multi-core score of 13,967. High I/O and caching performance is demonstrated by 30.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 31.29 GB/s static web serving throughput. While lacking dedicated GPUs and showing limited capacity for 70B parameter LLM inference, its balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and high-speed local disk make it effective for high-performance databases, caching layers, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
